name: The Quarry's Smith

angles.text: Frast Dokner serves as a field mentor for apprentice smiths, trading his hard-won forging techniques to anyone willing to supply the raw metal and leather required to keep his anvil hot.
Miners working the surrounding deposits will find an immediate local consumer for their smelted copper bars, turning raw ore into practical training and camp repairs.
Gol'Bolar Quarry represents Bronzebeard enterprise and industry in Dun Morogh, where dwarven resolve keeps the forges burning even when supply caravans run late.
Assisting Dokner ensures the remote dwarven quarry remains operational, bolstering local infrastructure and equipment readiness in the snowy high country.

faq.answer: Frast Dokner is an experienced blacksmith stationed at a quarry encampment, responsible for maintaining tools, structural fittings, and equipment for the workers on-site. When logistical delays cut off his regular supply line, he takes matters into his own hands by recruiting passing adventurers to secure the raw materials he desperately requires.

aliases: why copper bars and boar hides
faq.answer: Excavation and camp maintenance consume massive amounts of sturdy material. Copper provides an accessible, malleable metal suitable for forging replacement fittings, nails, fasteners, and reinforcing bands for broken tools. Toughened boar hides provide resilient leather necessary for bellows, tool wraps, straps, and protective aprons that withstand the harsh sparks and heavy grinding of daily quarry labor.
faq.q: Why does the quarry need copper bars and boar hides?

faq.answer: While Frast Dokner does not elaborate on the specific cause of the delay, overland supply routes across the snowy crags and mountain passes are frequently plagued by harsh blizzards, roving wildlife, and hostile trogg or bandit ambushes. Remote mining camps and quarries are often the first settlements to feel the strain whenever transport wagons fall behind schedule.
faq.q: Why is the supply shipment late?

faq.answer: Rather than offering coin alone, Frast Dokner promises to share his personal blacksmithing techniques with whoever gathers his needed supplies. For an aspiring artisan, learning directly from a seasoned craftsman stationed in the field offers practical insights into metalworking and equipment maintenance that formal city guildhalls rarely teach to novices.
faq.q: What does Frast Dokner offer in exchange for the materials?

faq.answer: Frast Dokner operates in Dun Morogh at Gol'Bolar Quarry, a dwarven excavation site nestled in the snowy foothills south of Kharanos. The quarry faces constant operational pressures from harsh winter weather and aggressive subterranean troggs that routinely harass the miners and disrupt trade convoys traveling from Ironforge.

aliases: is the quarry part of ironforge
faq.answer: Yes, Frast Dokner and the quarry encampment operate under the domain of the Bronzebeard clan and the Kingdom of Ironforge. Quarrying stone and extracting ore from the mountains of Dun Morogh are vital to the dwarven kingdom's construction projects and defensive fortifications, making local blacksmiths like Dokner essential to Ironforge's industrial strength.
faq.q: Is Frast Dokner affiliated with Ironforge?

sections.body: Life at an active excavation demands constant maintenance, from sharpening pickaxes and replacing worn brackets to reinforcing camp gear. When a vital supply shipment fails to arrive on schedule, daily work grinds toward a halt. Without fresh stock from the major trade routes, craftsmen on-site are forced to improvise and look to passing adventurers to keep the camp functional. Frast Dokner, working the forge amid these ongoing delays, relies on anyone willing to scrounge up basic metals and hides rather than waiting idly for transport wagons that may be hopelessly delayed.
sections.title: Shortages at the Quarry

sections.body: Traditional dwarven blacksmithing guilds prize discipline and closely guarded methods, rarely handing down trade secrets to casual wanderers. Dokner, however, balances local necessity against formal guild etiquette. Facing an immediate shortage of workable copper and durable leather needed for patching tools and camp gear, he offers a pragmatic trade: bring the raw materials directly to his anvil, and he will instruct you in his personal smithing techniques. It is a mutually beneficial bargain born of frontier necessity, trading valuable vocational knowledge for immediate survival and upkeep.
sections.title: An Apprentice's Bargain

summary: The Quarry's Smith is an arrangement offered by Frast Dokner, a working craftsman stationed at a quarry camp. Stranded without an expected supply delivery, the smith turns to willing travelers to gather raw metal and sturdy leather for essential camp repairs. In exchange for the needed materials, Dokner shares practical smithing techniques with aspiring metalworkers.
